memory_bridge: Turn the lone stroke into a winner’s podium: the formal number-one ribbon is 一番 for On イチ, while one small object sitting alone is counted 一つ for Kun ひとつ.

readings.overlay: Lay the single stroke across the first-place podium labeled 一番（いちばん）; its opening sound fixes On イチ as “number one.”
Place one apple on the lone stroke and count it 一つ（ひとつ）; the complete native counter word fixes Kun ひとつ, “one.”

memory_bridge: Lay the three strokes across March: 三月 supplies formal On サン, while three dumplings placed on the strokes are counted 三つ for native Kun みっつ.

readings.overlay: Print 三月（さんがつ） across the three-line March calendar; the opening sound fixes On サン in “March.”
Place one dumpling on each of the three strokes and count 三つ（みっつ）; the complete native counter fixes Kun みっつ, “three.”

memory_bridge: Build a five-level lift around the upper stroke: the formal sign 以上 uses On ジョウ; the top platform itself is 上 with Kun うえ; an operator raises a box with 上げる, the box rises with 上がる, and a climber ascends with 上る. The vertical motion is shared, but each full verb keeps agency and nuance clear.

readings.overlay: Bolt an 以上（いじょう） sign to the upper platform—“at least; above”; the final character supplies On ジョウ.
Stand on the higher stroke and point to the place 上（うえ）, “above”; the standalone native location word fixes Kun うえ.
Pull the lift lever and deliberately 上げる（あげる） a box to the top; the complete transitive verb fixes Kun あげる, “to raise.”
Release the lever and watch the platform itself 上がる（あがる）; the complete intransitive verb fixes Kun あがる, “to rise.”
Finally, have a climber scale the vertical line and 上る（のぼる） to the platform; the complete native verb fixes Kun のぼる, “to ascend.”

memory_bridge: Organize the dense family into three panels. SIGNS: 以下 uses On カ for a limit below, while a conductor calls GET OFF at 下車 to retrieve On ゲ. POSITION AND LEVERS: 下（した） is below; someone 下げる（さげる） an object, while it 下がる（さがる） by itself. DOWNWARD PATHS: a traveler 下る（くだる） a route or 下りる（おりる） from a vehicle; a respected person above 下さる（くださる） a gift. The panels separate location, agency, travel, and honorific giving.

readings.overlay: A limit line labeled 以下（いか） keeps every allowed amount at or below it. The exact word “at most; below” anchors On カ without the weak CAP fragment.
The conductor calls GET OFF as the passenger 下車（げしゃ）. The opening sound of GET retrieves On ゲ, and the compound means “get off a vehicle.”
Place the lower platform directly beneath the baseline and label the position 下（した）—below. The standalone location word anchors した.
A worker pulls a lever and 下げる（さげる） the platform—lowers it. Someone acts on the object, so this is transitive.
Release the lever and the platform 下がる（さがる）—goes down by itself. This is the intransitive partner.
A traveler follows the mountain road downward and 下る（くだる）—descends along it. The route scene distinguishes this from merely being below.
A respected person above lowers a gift into your hands and 下さる（くださる） it—honorifically gives it. Keep this social register attached to the full verb.
The passenger steps down from the train and 下りる（おりる）—gets off. The vehicle-exit scene distinguishes it from descending a route with くだる.

memory_bridge: Use the line through the middle as a border map: the labeled nation 中国 gives On チュウ, while a treasure sitting physically inside the box is 中 for Kun なか.

readings.overlay: Turn the centered box into a map stamped 中国（ちゅうごく）; its first character sounds On チュウ in “China.”
Hide a coin at the exact center of the box and point to the 中（なか）, “inside”; the bare native noun fixes Kun なか.

memory_bridge: On シュ names a master in compounds; Kun おも marks what is main, while ぬし identifies an owner.

readings.overlay: The marked king fits the master’s shoe before greeting 主人（しゅじん）; shoe → シュ, the On reading.
Place the marked king in the center and everyone else at the edge: 主に（おもに）, ‘mainly.’
The person holding the king’s marked property is its 持ち主（もちぬし）, ‘owner’; 主 carries ぬし there.

memory_bridge: キュウ is the general On count, ク is the fixed clock reading in 九時, and ここのつ is the complete native counter word for nine things.

readings.overlay: Nine is the cue to hook the last single digit before ten; cue → キュウ in 九（きゅう）.
At nine o’clock a cuckoo clock gives one clipped ‘ku!’; 九時（くじ）uses On ク.
Place nine counters around the hooked numeral and count the entire native bundle aloud: 九つ（ここのつ）, ‘nine things.’

memory_bridge: Pin two tags to the matter in the hand: the breaking-news tag says 事件 for On ジ, while the ordinary thing being handled is simply 事 for Kun こと.

readings.overlay: Make the gripped marker flash as a newsworthy 事件（じけん）, “event”; the compound begins with On ジ.
When the flashing stops, hold up the matter itself and call it a 事（こと）, “thing”; the standalone native noun fixes Kun こと.

memory_bridge: Turn the two strokes into a February calendar shelf: 二月 supplies formal On ニ, while two objects placed on the two shelves are 二つ for Kun ふたつ.

readings.overlay: Write 二月（にがつ） across the two-line February calendar; the opening sound fixes On ニ in “February.”
Set one orange on each stroke and count the pair 二つ（ふたつ）; the full native counter word fixes Kun ふたつ, “two.”

memory_bridge: Turn the five-point shape into a May picnic: 五月 on the invitation supplies On ゴ, while five rice balls counted at the picnic are 五つ for Kun いつつ.

readings.overlay: Pin 五月（ごがつ） to the five-point calendar as the May page; its opening sound fixes On ゴ.
Place a rice ball at each of the five built-in points and count 五つ（いつつ）; the complete native counter fixes Kun いつつ, “five.”
Place the capital scene at the eastern edge of a map and label it 東京（とうきょう）; the famous city name fixes 京 as On キョウ.

memory_bridge: Stage three people around the two-legged figure: a Japanese person wears a 日本人 badge for On ジン, a headcount of three uses 三人 for On ニン, and one ordinary person alone answers to 人 for Kun ひと.

readings.overlay: Pin 日本人（にほんじん） to the standing figure like a nationality badge; its last character sounds On ジン and means “Japanese person.”
Now line up exactly three figures and let the counter call 三人（さんにん）; the counting reading is On ニン, “three people.”
Leave one figure standing by itself and introduce that person simply as 人（ひと）; the native noun gives Kun ひと.

memory_bridge: Under the person-roof, hold a card for 今回 with On コン, then tear away the card and point to the present instant 今 with Kun いま.

readings.overlay: Hang 今回（こんかい）, “this time,” from the roof like an event card; the first character begins with On コン.
Drop the event card, clap at the immediate moment, and say 今（いま）; the standalone native word fixes Kun いま, “now.”

memory_bridge: On ダイ counts eras or generations. 代わる（かわる）is to take another’s role, while 代える（かえる）is to replace one thing with another.

readings.overlay: Each generation rolls a new die before inheriting the halberd; die → ダイ in 時代（じだい）, an era.
One person steps away and another takes over the inherited halberd: 代わる（かわる）, ‘to succeed or substitute for.’
A hand removes the worn halberd and replaces it with a new one: 代える（かえる）, ‘to replace.’

memory_bridge: Under the meeting roof, first see the organization that owns it—会社 for On カイ—then watch two people actually meet and say 会う for Kun あう.

readings.overlay: Hang the 会社（かいしゃ） company sign over the crowded meeting roof; its first character is read with On カイ.
Two people enter from opposite sides, greet beneath the roof, and 会う（あう）—the full native verb fixes Kun あう, “to meet.”

memory_bridge: On タイ belongs to experience and other body compounds; Kun からだ is the standalone native word ‘body.’

readings.overlay: Tie a book to the person’s head and let the whole body experience balancing it: tie → タイ in 体験（たいけん）.
Remove the book and attend to the person’s whole physical frame: 体（からだ）, native ‘body.’
March all the human legs behind a 政党（せいとう） campaign banner; the final character uses On トウ in “political party.”

memory_bridge: A new pupil retrieves On ニュウ. For the native pair, the person goes in with 入る（はいる）; the hand puts an object in with 入れる（いれる）.

readings.overlay: A new pupil funnels through the school doorway: ‘new entry’ cues ニュウ in 入学（にゅうがく）, entering school.
The child walks through the narrowing strokes under their own power: 入る（はいる）, ‘to enter.’
Now the child picks up a book and puts it through the doorway: 入れる（いれる）, ‘to put in.’

memory_bridge: The Zen king retrieves compound On ゼン; every subject sheltered under the roof retrieves the complete native word 全て（すべて）.

readings.overlay: The king sits peacefully under the shelter with his whole Zen kingdom intact: Zen → ゼン in 全部（ぜんぶ）, ‘all.’
Gather every last subject beneath the royal roof—nothing remains outside: 全て（すべて）, ‘everything.’

memory_bridge: On ハチ is the regular compound reading; Kun 八つ（やっつ）is the complete native counter word for eight things.

readings.overlay: Eight eggs hatch under the August calendar page; hatch → ハチ in 八月（はちがつ）.
Divide eight counters into two groups of four, then count the full native set: 八つ（やっつ）, ‘eight things.’

memory_bridge: A ROCK holds down the 六月 calendar page, retrieving On ロク; lifting it reveals six MITTS, arranged as three pairs, retrieving native 六つ（むっつ）.

readings.overlay: A ROCK holds down the June page 六月（ろくがつ）. ROCK closely retrieves On ロク.
Under the rock are six MITTS arranged as three pairs. MITTS closely retrieves むっつ in the complete counter 六つ（むっつ）.

memory_bridge: Keep the person enclosed by the frame: a national map labels the area 国内 with On ナイ, while the person points to the interior itself as 内 with Kun うち.

readings.overlay: Draw the enclosing frame as a national border and shade 国内（こくない）, “domestic; within the country”; the final character uses On ナイ.
Have the enclosed person tap the space around them and say 内（うち）, “inside”; the standalone native noun fixes Kun うち.
Trace the round coin and place it in a till marked 円（えん）. The everyday currency word itself is the reliable anchor for On エン.

memory_bridge: Use one departure door to contrast agency: 出る is the passenger going out, while 出す is the passenger putting a suitcase out. Above both, 出発 names the departure itself with canonical シュツ, compressed to しゅっ in しゅっぱつ.

readings.overlay: The 出発（しゅっぱつ） board flashes over the exit. Canonical シュツ compresses to しゅっ before 発, so the visible word teaches both the reading and its common surface form.
The passenger personally crosses the threshold and 出る（でる）—leaves. No object is moved; the person goes out.
The passenger reaches back and 出す（だす） the suitcase—takes it out. Here someone moves an object through the same door.

memory_bridge: Let the knife divide a day-planner into four labeled slices: 自分 for On ブン points to oneself, 五分 for On フン measures five minutes, 分かる for Kun わかる is the moment a puzzle becomes understood, and 分ける for Kun わける physically divides the pieces. The cutting image organizes them without collapsing their distinct senses.

readings.overlay: Hand one of the eight cut pieces to yourself and label it 自分（じぶん）; the final character uses On ブン in “myself.”
Set the knife-timer to 五分（ごふん）, “five minutes”; the counter reading of the final character is On フン.
Fit the divided puzzle pieces together until the answer clicks and you 分かる（わかる）; the complete native verb fixes Kun わかる, “to understand.”
Use the knife to sort the pieces into separate bowls and 分ける（わける）; the complete transitive verb fixes Kun わける, “to divide.”

memory_bridge: Use the grass-clearing knife as a clock hand: before noon it marks 午前 with On ゼン, while its physical position ahead of you is 前 with Kun まえ.

readings.overlay: Before the knife reaches the top of the clock, hang 午前（ごぜん） over the cleared grass; the word “morning” ends with On ゼン.
Place the knife one pace ahead and point to the space 前（まえ）, “in front”; the standalone native location word fixes Kun まえ.

memory_bridge: On リョク names ability, On リキ powers the sumo compound, and Kun ちから is the native standalone word for strength.

readings.overlay: The hooked arm proves what it can do on an ability gauge labeled 能力（のうりょく）; the power character carries On リョク there.
Ricky the sumo wrestler flexes the hooked arm before entering the ring: Ricky → リキ in 力士（りきし）.
Strip away the uniform and title; the raw force in the flexing arm itself is 力（ちから）, native ‘strength; power.’

memory_bridge: On ドウ moves inside compounds. 動く（うごく）means something moves, while 動かす（うごかす）means someone moves something.

readings.overlay: A heavy lump of dough suddenly moves like an animal: dough → ドウ in 動物（どうぶつ）.
The heavy object begins shifting under its own power: 動く（うごく）, intransitive ‘to move.’
A person applies force and makes the heavy object shift: 動かす（うごかす）, transitive ‘to move something.’

memory_bridge: Use three transformations: a cultural display is 文化 with On カ; a face changes through 化粧 with On ケ; a person transforms or disguises themself with 化ける（ばける）.

readings.overlay: Standing and inverted figures fill a 文化（ぶんか） exhibit. The familiar word “culture” anchors On カ.
A makeup brush changes the face through 化粧（けしょう）. This distinctive common word anchors alternate On ケ.
The figure flips and 化ける（ばける）—transforms or disguises themself. The complete verb anchors ばける without the loose BAKER comparison.

memory_bridge: Use the crossed ten-tally at a feast: ten servings make the guests say 十分 for On ジュウ, while counting all ten pieces one by one ends with 十 for Kun とお.

readings.overlay: Pile food around the crossed tally until everyone says 十分（じゅうぶん）, “enough”; its first character supplies On ジュウ.
Count the ten tally pieces to the end and name the total 十（とお）; the standalone native count fixes Kun とお, “ten.”

memory_bridge: Use two matching mouth-shaped pieces in three steps: their total is written 合計 with On ゴウ; by themselves they come together with 合う, Kun あう; and a person actively aligns them with 合わせる, Kun あわせる.

readings.overlay: Count the fitted pieces on a receipt labeled 合計（ごうけい）, “sum total”; the first character uses On ゴウ.
Let the two curved pieces slide together until they 合う（あう）; the complete native verb fixes Kun あう, “to come together.”
Now have a musician deliberately align two beats and 合わせる（あわせる） their rhythm; the complete native verb fixes Kun あわせる, “to match.”

memory_bridge: Under the common cover, synchronize two clocks for 同時 with On ドウ, then have every mouth give 同じ as the native Kun おなじ answer. Both scenes share sameness but preserve the compound and adjective.

readings.overlay: Put two clocks under the cover and make them strike at 同時（どうじ）, “the same time”; the compound begins with On ドウ.
Ask the covered mouths a question and hear the 同じ（おなじ） answer from each; the full native adjective fixes Kun おなじ, “same.”
At payroll, each employee steps in when their name is called and receives a shell: company employee 会社員（かいしゃいん）ends in On イン.

memory_bridge: The monster behind the gate retrieves On モン and its test question; the toe knocking on the gate retrieves native 問う（とう）.

readings.overlay: A monster behind the gate holds up a test question; monster → モン in 問題（もんだい）.
A toe knocks on the closed gate before the mouth asks who is outside: toe → とう in 問う（とう）, ‘to ask.’

memory_bridge: Make the four-sided enclosure a spring calendar and counting tray: 四月 supplies On シ, the bare numeral 四 supplies Kun よん, and four objects counted with the native counter are 四つ for Kun よっつ.

readings.overlay: Paste 四月（しがつ） inside the four-sided April calendar; the opening character uses On シ.
Write the bare number 四（よん） at the center of the four sides; the standalone numeral fixes Kun よん, “four.”
Put one flower on each side and count the set 四つ（よっつ）; the complete native counter word fixes Kun よっつ, “four.”

memory_bridge: Send an echo around the enclosure three ways: 今回 counts “this time” with On カイ; the echo itself circles back with 回る, Kun まわる; and a hand turns the enclosure with 回す, Kun まわす. The circular image distinguishes self-turning from actively turning something.

readings.overlay: Stamp 今回（こんかい）, “this time,” each time the echo completes a circuit; the final character uses On カイ.
Watch the echo travel around the enclosure by itself and 回る（まわる）; the complete intransitive verb fixes Kun まわる, “to turn.”
Reach in with a hand and actively spin the inner mouth, 回す（まわす）; the complete transitive verb fixes Kun まわす, “to turn.”

memory_bridge: Keep three meanings on one planning desk. A ZOO is circled on 地図（ちず）, map—ZOO retrieves ズ. A heavy TOME rolls toward 図書館（としょかん）, library—TOME begins with ト. A planner measures the route before 図る（はかる）, planning it. Map, library, and plan remain word-specific rather than being treated as one definition.

readings.overlay: Circle a ZOO on 地図（ちず）, the map. ZOO closely retrieves On ズ, while 地図 supplies the exact common-word meaning “map.”
A heavy TOME rolls into 図書館（としょかん）, the library. The opening sound of TOME retrieves On ト; the anchor’s meaning remains “library.”
The planner measures every route and then 図る（はかる）—plans or attempts—the project. The complete verb supplies its own usage-specific meaning rather than inheriting “map.”

memory_bridge: Use the protected country as a border checkpoint: the passport from a foreign country says 外国 for On コク, while the land inside the enclosure calls itself 国 for Kun くに.

readings.overlay: At the jade-guarded border, stamp 外国（がいこく） on a foreign passport; the ending On sound is コク, and the compound means “foreign country.”
Inside the enclosure, point to the whole protected land and name it 国（くに）; the standalone native word gives Kun くに, “country.”

memory_bridge: Spread the ground into a folded map: the printed 地図 uses On チ, while unfolding it onto the actual 地面 switches the same character to On ジ. The paper and terrain scenes keep the two compound readings distinct.

readings.overlay: Draw roads across the earth and fold it into a 地図（ちず）, “map”; the first character is read On チ.
Drop the map and let it land flat on 地面（じめん）, the “ground”; the first character now takes On ジ.

memory_bridge: On ジョウ places 場 inside compounds such as an assembly hall; Kun ば names a place in native vocabulary.

readings.overlay: Joe steps onto the sunlit earth and welcomes a whole assembly into 会場（かいじょう）; Joe cues the compound reading ジョウ.
Drive a flag marked ば into that exact patch of earth; it becomes the ば of 場所（ばしょ）, a ‘place.’

memory_bridge: The foreign guy retrieves On ガイ. Outside, そと is the physical location and ほか points elsewhere; a hand 外す（はずす）the tablet, while a failed clasp lets it 外れる（はずれる）.

readings.overlay: A foreign guy carries the divination table beyond the border at dusk: guy → ガイ in 外国（がいこく）.
Set the table beyond the doorway under the dusk sky; that physical outside is 外（そと）.
The diviner rejects this spot and points elsewhere, to 外（ほか）, ‘another place; something else.’
Unhook the divination tablet from its mount and remove it: 外す（はずす）, transitive ‘to take off.’
The tablet’s clasp fails and it comes loose by itself: 外れる（はずれる）, intransitive ‘to come off; be disconnected.’

memory_bridge: Let the arms-wide giant tour a campus: the entrance arch says 大学 for On ダイ, the giant carefully protects something 大切 for On タイ, and his sheer size is 大きい for Kun おおきい.

readings.overlay: The arms-wide figure becomes a campus gate marked 大学（だいがく）; the first character sounds On ダイ in “university.”
Inside, the giant cradles one important object labeled 大切（たいせつ）; this word gives the other On sound タイ and means “important.”
Zoom out until the spreading figure fills the frame and exclaim 大きい（おおきい）; the complete adjective fixes Kun おおきい, “big.”

memory_bridge: Shrink the child until SHE rides an electric spark in 電子, retrieving On シ; restore the child to ordinary size for the complete native word 子供（こども）.

readings.overlay: Shrink the waving child until SHE rides an electric spark in 電子（でんし）, “electron.” SHE closely retrieves On シ.
Restore the child to ordinary size and let the child wave in 子供（こども）. The common word “child” honestly anchors Kun こ without the mismatched COAT cue.

memory_bridge: At one desk, the learner wears a 学生（がくせい） badge for compound On ガク, then works through the lesson by hand and 学ぶ（まなぶ）—learns.

readings.overlay: The child takes a seat as a 学生（がくせい）—student. This foundational word anchors On ガク more honestly than the mismatched English GAWK.
The child works through the lesson step by step and 学ぶ（まなぶ）—learns. The complete native verb is the anchor.

memory_bridge: Under the chosen roof, first pin a calendar plan 予定 for On テイ, then have the straight foot make the actual decision with 定める for Kun さだめる.

readings.overlay: Pin 予定（よてい）, “plans,” above the roof before choosing it; the final character uses On テイ.
Have the straight foot point decisively to one roof and 定める（さだめる） it; the complete native verb fixes Kun さだめる, “to decide.”

memory_bridge: A reality stamp retrieves On ジツ through 実際; the single fruit is み, while fruit appearing across the trellis is the event 実る（みのる）.

readings.overlay: The planned house receives a bold REALITY stamp reading 実際（じっさい）; the compound surfaces On ジツ as じっ before さ.
Inside the now-real house sits one small fruit meant for me: me → み, the standalone fruit 実（み）.
The roof becomes a trellis, heavy with ripening fruit: 実る（みのる）, ‘to bear fruit.’
Put the mirrored writing on opposing protest signs marked 反対（はんたい）; the compound ends with On タイ and means “opposition.”

memory_bridge: Under the market awning, a 市民 badge gives formal On シ, while the old-fashioned market call 市場 starts with native Kun いち.

readings.overlay: Give a shopper beneath the cloth awning a 市民（しみん） badge; the first character’s On シ identifies a “citizen.”
Have the vendor open the town 市場（いちば） and call the first character いち; that complete market word fixes Kun いち.

memory_bridge: Keep the harvest cycle as a two-turn calendar: the next harvest is 来年 for On ネン, while one year experienced as a span is 年 for Kun とし.

readings.overlay: Tie a 来年（らいねん） tag to next season’s unripe grain; the compound ends in On ネン and means “next year.”
After the person finishes one full harvest cycle, call that span a 年（とし）; the standalone native noun fixes Kun とし, “year.”

memory_bridge: At the target range, a TOE stamps 本当, true—retrieving On トウ. Then contrast outcomes: the arrow 当たる（あたる）—hits or proves correct—while the archer 当てる（あてる） it by aiming or guessing.

readings.overlay: A TOE presses the truth-stamp into 本当（ほんとう）. TOE closely retrieves On トウ in the word “true.”
The released arrow 当たる（あたる）—hits the mark—and the prediction proves correct. The complete intransitive verb is the anchor.
The archer deliberately aims and 当てる（あてる） the mark—or guesses correctly. The complete transitive verb contrasts with the result 当たる.

memory_bridge: Keep the thread-delayed walker behind a moving clock: 午後 marks the afternoon with On ゴ, 後 points to what comes later with Kun あと, and 後ろ points to the space at the back with Kun うしろ.

readings.overlay: The delayed walker finally arrives when the clock reads 午後（ごご）, “afternoon”; the second character repeats the On sound ゴ.
Leave a note on the path saying “come later” and label that later point 後（あと）; the standalone native word fixes Kun あと, “after; later.”
Look back and find the thread-tangled foot still 後ろ（うしろ）, at the back; the complete native location word fixes Kun うしろ.
A meaningful sound rises from the heart as a clear ‘ee’; that イ begins 意味（いみ）, ‘meaning.’

memory_bridge: The battlefield has two anchors: the formal conflict is 戦争（せんそう） with On セン; in the foreground, halberds strike TA-TA before the fighters 戦う（たたかう）.

readings.overlay: A declaration crosses the battlefield and begins 戦争（せんそう）—war. The exact compound anchors On セン without pretending English SEND is the same sound.
Halberds strike TA-TA before the fighters 戦う（たたかう）. The repeated impact sound retrieves the opening たた of the complete verb “to fight.”

memory_bridge: A flying SHOE lands in the chosen player’s 手, retrieving シュ in 選手; when the shoe is removed, the hand itself is simply 手（て）.

readings.overlay: The 選手（せんしゅ） catches a flying SHOE in one outstretched hand. SHOE closely retrieves On シュ in the word “player.”
Remove the shoe and focus on the pictured hand itself: 手（て）. The standalone native noun is the complete anchor for Kun て.
At the ballot scene, hang a 政治（せいじ） banner over the correct choice; the opening On セイ names the compound “politics.”

memory_bridge: A bumped shin retrieves On シン and its newspaper; opening the finished home reveals the complete native adjective 新しい（あたらしい）.

readings.overlay: While cutting lumber for the new home, a parent bangs a shin; the dropped 新聞（しんぶん）links that shin sound to On シン.
They swing the axe-cut door open and admire every untouched beam: 新しい（あたらしい）, the full native adjective ‘new.’

memory_bridge: Use the knife as a compass pointer: an instruction card shows 方法 for On ホウ, while the direction it physically points is 方 for Kun かた.

readings.overlay: Tie a step-by-step 方法（ほうほう） card to the knife-compass; the repeated first character uses On ホウ in “method.”
Remove the instruction card and follow the blade’s pointing 方（かた）, “direction”; the standalone native noun fixes Kun かた.

memory_bridge: Let the square sun become a three-page calendar: 日曜日 is the Sunday page for On ニチ, 本日 is the TODAY stamp for On ジツ, and the warm daylight itself is native ひ. The shared sun image orders the readings without pretending Sunday, today, and day are the same word.

readings.overlay: Circle 日曜日（にちようび） on the sun calendar and read the first character aloud: On ニチ marks Sunday.
Stamp 本日（ほんじつ） across today’s sunlit page; the final stamp sound is On ジツ, and the word means “today.”
Step out under the pictured sun and call the day itself 日（ひ）; this bare native word gives Kun ひ.

memory_bridge: Keep the sun-and-moon scene on one timeline: an explanation becomes clear in 説明 with メイ; the next morning is 明朝 with ミョウ; the sky is 明るい while bright, then night 明ける as dawn breaks.

readings.overlay: MAY switches on both sun and moon until the explanation is clear: 説明（せつめい）. MAY closely retrieves On メイ.
Sun and moon exchange places at tomorrow morning’s horizon: 明朝（みょうちょう）. That exact “tomorrow morning” compound anchors On ミョウ.
With sun and moon flooding the scene with light, the whole sky is 明るい（あかるい）—bright. Keep the complete adjective as the anchor.
The moon’s watch ends as the sun breaks through and night 明ける（あける）—dawns or comes to an end.

memory_bridge: At the sunlit temple clock, a formal schedule measures 時間 with On ジ, while someone asks for the moment itself—時 with Kun とき.

readings.overlay: Hang a timetable marked 時間（じかん） from the temple clock; its first character sounds On ジ in the word “time.”
Freeze the sun at one precise moment and name that moment 時（とき）; the standalone native word fixes Kun とき, “time.”

memory_bridge: At the awards table, the latest prize comes with a SIGH for 最近, retrieving On サイ; the top prize is simply labeled 最も（もっとも）, most.

readings.overlay: At sunset the winner gives a SIGH while taking the latest prize in 最近（さいきん）, “recently.” SIGH closely retrieves On サイ.
The top-ranked prize is 最も（もっとも） valuable—most valuable. The complete native word anchors もっとも without assembling it from the English word “motto.”

memory_bridge: Turn the crescent into a calendar dial: point to 月曜日 for On ゲツ, flip to 一月 for On ガツ, then lift the dial into the night sky and call the moon 月 for Kun つき.

readings.overlay: Circle 月曜日（げつようび） beneath the crescent on the weekly dial; its first character sounds On ゲツ in “Monday.”
Flip the same moon dial to 一月（いちがつ）, “January”; the final character now uses the calendar-month On sound ガツ.
Lift the crescent off the calendar and into the sky, naming the celestial body 月（つき）; the standalone native word fixes Kun つき, “Moon.”

memory_bridge: At the marked tree root, bind its paper into a 本 read with On ホン, then point back to the root itself as 本 read with Kun もと. One image connects book material to origin while the two whole words keep the senses apart.

readings.overlay: Pulp the marked tree into pages and bind them as a 本（ほん）; this standalone book word is read with On ホン.
Peel the pages back into wood and tap the marked base—the 本（もと）, “origin”; that contrasting native word fixes Kun もと.

memory_bridge: Let the sun brighten the eastern tree twice: first as the skyline of 東京 for On トウ, then as the compass direction 東 for Kun ひがし.

readings.overlay: Grow the eastern tree into the skyline of 東京（とうきょう）; the city name begins with On トウ.
Turn from the skyline to the sunrise itself and point 東（ひがし）; the standalone native direction word fixes Kun ひがし, “east.”
Let the tender business shoot mature into a tower labeled 企業（きぎょう）; the final character sounds On ギョウ in “enterprise.”

memory_bridge: On シ appears in formal name compounds; Kun うじ is the older native word for a clan or family name.

readings.overlay: She presses the inherited clan seal beside her full name: she → シ in 氏名（しめい）.
An old family gathers around the curled seal and recites its lineage: 氏（うじ）, ‘clan; family name.’
At the eye-by-eye census, stamp every counted resident 国民（こくみん）; the final On sound ミン names the “people of a country.”

memory_bridge: At one decision board, the official result is 決定 with canonical ケツ compressed to けっ; a voter 決める（きめる） the choice, and after the vote the result 決まる（きまる）.

readings.overlay: The final choice receives the 決定（けってい） stamp. Canonical ケツ compresses to けっ before テイ; the word shows the real surface form without the weak GETS pun.
A voter points to one option and 決める（きめる） it—decides. This is the transitive act that produces the result.
After the vote, the result 決まる（きまる）—is decided. This intransitive scene contrasts with the voter deciding it.
The engineer pins step-by-step instructions beside the water channel: 方法（ほうほう）, “method.” The repeated common compound is the honest anchor for On ホウ; English HOW does not closely reproduce it.

memory_bridge: At one exhibit, 現在（げんざい） marks what is present now; the hidden jade 現れる（あらわれる） by itself, while the curator 現す（あらわす） it deliberately.

readings.overlay: A placard says the jade is on display 現在（げんざい）—at present. The common time word anchors On ゲン without the phonetically inaccurate GEM cue.
The hidden jade 現れる（あらわれる）—appears—when the cover falls away by itself. This is the intransitive event.
A curator deliberately 現す（あらわす） the jade—reveals or represents it. This is the transitive action.
The traveler returns the jade and writes the 理由（りゆう）—reason—for the trip. The exact common word anchors On リ without depending on an English L/R approximation.

memory_bridge: Follow one sprout through distinct forms of life: its everyday 生活 is セイ; its whole 一生 is ショウ; while alive it 生きる, when first appearing it 生まれる, and before processing it remains 生, as in 生ビール. Each complete word supplies the meaning specific to that reading.

readings.overlay: Build a small home around the thriving sprout and watch its daily 生活（せいかつ）—life. The first character is the On anchor セイ.
Stretch a ribbon from the sprout’s first leaf to its final season: 一生（いっしょう）, a whole life. 一 compresses to いっ; 生 itself realizes On ショウ.
Water the sprout and watch it continue to 生きる（いきる）—live. The complete verb preserves the okurigana and the active living sense.
A new shoot breaks through the soil and 生まれる（うまれる）—is born. The complete verb anchors the emergence meaning.
At the festival, fresh draft 生ビール（なまビール） pours straight from the tap. This unprocessed, fresh scene anchors Kun なま rather than a generic “life” gloss.

memory_bridge: On デン appears in agricultural compounds; Kun た is the native word for a rice field.

readings.overlay: Water fills all four plots, making a paddy as deep as a den: den → デン in 水田（すいでん）.
Viewed from above with no compound attached, the four plots themselves are 田（た）, a rice field.
The train springs away under 出発（しゅっぱつ）, “departure.” Canonical ハツ surfaces as ぱつ after the small っ, so しゅっぱつ is the real-word anchor and the sound change is explicit.

memory_bridge: A MOCK eye exam marks one objective in 目的, retrieving On モク; after the exam, remove the chart and name the eye itself 目（め）.

readings.overlay: A MOCK eye exam asks you to focus on one marked objective in 目的（もくてき）. MOCK closely retrieves On モク.
After the chart comes down, point to the eye itself: 目（め）. The standalone native noun is the anchor; English “me” would cue み, not め.

memory_bridge: Let the tree and eye face a companion across a consultation table: the formal meeting is 相談 for On ソウ, while the person opposite is 相手 for Kun あい.

readings.overlay: Seat the tree and watchful eye at a 相談（そうだん） table; the word “consultation” begins with On ソウ.
Place a trusted companion opposite the watching eye and label that counterpart 相手（あいて）; the first character uses Kun あい.
Turn the earth-planted community shrine into the lobby of a 会社（かいしゃ）; the company sign ends with On シャ.

memory_bridge: On リツ stands inside compounds; 立つ（たつ）is intransitive ‘stand,’ while 立てる（たてる）is transitive ‘stand something up.’

readings.overlay: A national monument stands upright like the Ritz tower: 国立（こくりつ）ends with On リツ.
The person plants their own feet on the ground and stands: 立つ（たつ）, the native intransitive action.
The person lifts a fallen sign and stands it up: 立てる（たてる）, the native transitive action.

memory_bridge: The bay crossing retrieves On ベイ and America; the bowl at home retrieves the native grain-word 米（こめ）.

readings.overlay: Four rice grains sail across a bay toward the United States; bay → ベイ in 米国（べいこく）.
Back home, the four scattered grains gather into a bowl: 米（こめ）, the native word for husked rice.
A yak ties the ladle to its horn so it must be returned; yak → ヤク in 約束（やくそく）, a binding promise.
Kay follows the sage’s thread through every teaching, gaining 経験（けいけん）, ‘experience’; her name cues On ケイ.

memory_bridge: Give the sun-aged person two roles: in a white coat the person is 医者 for On シャ, while without a title the person is 者 for Kun もの.

readings.overlay: Dress the sun-aged person in a white coat and introduce an 医者（いしゃ）; the final character sounds On シャ in “doctor.”
Remove the coat and point simply to the person as 者（もの）; the standalone native noun fixes Kun もの, “person.”

memory_bridge: Keep the finger pointing at the same nose: on an ID form it labels 自分 with On ジ, while a deliberate self-introduction uses 自ら with Kun みずから.

readings.overlay: Beside the nose-pointing figure, fill in 自分（じぶん） on the “myself” line; the first character supplies On ジ.
Have the figure step forward and do the task 自ら（みずから）, “oneself”; the complete native expression fixes Kun みずから.

memory_bridge: Four stations keep the meanings apart: COACH → コウ action; ギョウザ → ギョウ line; EEK → いく go; ceremony → おこなう perform.

readings.overlay: At the 行動（こうどう） starting gate, a COACH launches the action team. The opening sound of COACH retrieves On コウ; the anchor itself means “action.”
A ギョウザ cart rolls into the 行列（ぎょうれつ） queue. The exact opening sound of ギョウザ retrieves On ギョウ, while 行列 itself means “line.”
A spider blocks the fork; the traveler squeaks ‘Eek!’ and decides to 行く（いく）—go. The close EEK sound retrieves Kun いく from the complete verb.
At the final stage, the traveler carries out the planned ceremony: 行う（おこなう）, “to perform.” Keep the complete verb as the anchor rather than forcing an English pun.

memory_bridge: At one public display, 発表（はっぴょう） supplies On ヒョウ; its outward face is 表（おもて）; a designer 表す（あらわす） an idea, while an image 表れる（あらわれる） by itself.

readings.overlay: Pin an announcement poster over the opening: 発表（はっぴょう）. 発 contributes はっ, and ヒョウ surfaces as ぴょう after small っ; the alternation is part of the real-word anchor.
Turn the garment over and inspect its outward face: 表（おもて）, “surface; front.”
A designer deliberately pushes a symbol through the garment to 表す（あらわす） an idea—represent it.
The growing shoot breaks through by itself and 表れる（あらわれる）—appears. This is the intransitive event.

memory_bridge: Give the walking eye four roles, not four interchangeable glosses: it posts an 意見 opinion, actively 見る a painting, notices a mountain that 見える, then deliberately 見せる the painting to someone else. The full words distinguish opinion, seeing, visibility, and showing.

readings.overlay: The walking eye pins its 意見（いけん）—opinion—to a noticeboard; the compound’s final ケン is the On anchor.
The eye deliberately studies a painting: 見る（みる）, “to see.” The complete active verb anchors みる.
A distant mountain emerges on its own and 見える（みえる）—comes into view. The complete verb anchors みえる without assigning an agent who shows it.
The eye’s owner holds up the painting for another person and 見せる（みせる）—shows it. This is the transitive showing scene for みせる.

memory_bridge: Use one speech desk: its language manual is 言語（げんご） with On ゲン; the speaker 言う（いう） a sentence; each sentence becomes 言葉（ことば）, where 言 contributes こと.

readings.overlay: Marked sounds are organized into 言語（げんご）—language. That exact compound anchors On ゲン; “generate” was not a close enough sound cue.
The speaker opens their mouth and 言う（いう） the sentence—says it. The complete verb is the anchor; English “you” does not reproduce いう.
The utterance is written on a leaf as 言葉（ことば）, “word; language.” This common whole word anchors the bound reading こと.

memory_bridge: The investigation clipboard fixes compound On チョウ; examining each note one by one retrieves the complete native verb 調べる（しらべる）.

readings.overlay: Investigators circle the singer with a clipboard labeled 調査（ちょうさ）; that exact investigation compound fixes On チョウ.
The investigator listens to and records every vowel in the tune: 調べる（しらべる）, ‘to examine; investigate.’
Seat the righteous speakers around a 会議（かいぎ） table; the meeting word ends in On ギ, giving the sound to the act of deliberation.

memory_bridge: Use one road in three modes: 交通（こうつう） names traffic with On ツウ; a traveler 通る（とおる） through it, someone 通す（とおす） an object through it, and a commuter 通う（かよう） along it repeatedly.

readings.overlay: Two streams meet on the same road as 交通（こうつう）—traffic. The common compound anchors On ツウ; English TWO lacks the initial affricate and is not a sufficiently close cue.
A traveler 通る（とおる） the gate—passes through under their own motion. This is the intransitive path.
The traveler 通す（とおす） a long pole through the gate—passes something through. This is the transitive partner.
Footprints cover the same road there and back each day as the traveler 通う（かよう）—commutes or goes regularly.

memory_bridge: Drive the connecting vehicle through two linked scenes: it sends a 連絡 for On レン, then stops to take a companion along with 連れる for Kun つれる.

readings.overlay: String telephone wires behind the moving vehicle and send a 連絡（れんらく）, “contact”; the compound begins with On レン.
Stop the vehicle, invite a companion aboard, and 連れる（つれる） them with you; the complete native verb fixes Kun つれる.

memory_bridge: Use one selection table: the chosen athlete receives the 選手 badge with On セン; before that result exists, the coach must 選ぶ（えらぶ）—choose—from the candidates.

readings.overlay: The coach pins an 選手（せんしゅ） badge on the selected athlete. That common role word is the honest anchor for On セン.
Before pinning the badge, the coach compares the candidates and 選ぶ（えらぶ）—chooses—one of them.
Circle the spit-marked section on the city map and tear off that 部分（ぶぶん）, “portion”; each occurrence of the character carries On ブ.

memory_bridge: The family’s gold heirloom retrieves kin → On キン and its Friday square; the coins made from that gold retrieve standalone money 金（かね）.

readings.overlay: All the kin gather around the gold heirloom on Friday; kin → キン in 金曜日（きんようび）.
The gold plates become clinking coins in a cash drawer; that money is simply 金（かね）, Kun かね.

memory_bridge: Let the stretched figure become a very tall company president: his 社長 title uses On チョウ, while the visibly long ribbon trailing behind him is 長い with Kun ながい.

readings.overlay: Put a 社長（しゃちょう） nameplate on the tall stretched figure; the title “company president” ends with On チョウ.
Unroll his trailing ribbon across the room and call it 長い（ながい）; the full native adjective fixes Kun ながい, “long.”

memory_bridge: At an opening ceremony, 開始（かいし） names the start with On カイ. Then track agency and shape: a door 開く（あく） by itself, someone 開ける（あける） it, and a book or event 開く（ひらく） by spreading open.

readings.overlay: The curtains part under a 開始（かいし） sign and the event starts. The exact compound anchors On カイ without relying on the mismatched English “key.”
With no hand touching it, the door 開く（あく）—opens by itself. This is the intransitive scene.
A person pulls the latch and 開ける（あける） the door—opens it. This is the transitive scene.
A book spreads flat and 開く（ひらく）—opens out. The broad unfolding distinguishes it from the door pair.

memory_bridge: Open the sunlit gap in the gate onto four spaces: a clock hangs there for 時間 with On カン, a crowd beyond it is 世間 with On ケン, the measurable space between the doors is 間 with Kun あいだ, and a dramatic pause in that gap is 間 with Kun ま.

readings.overlay: Hang a clock in the sunlit gate gap and label the measured time 時間（じかん）; the final character uses On カン.
Swing the gate open onto the whole social world, 世間（せけん）; its final character uses the other On sound ケン.
Stretch a tape measure across the space between the two doors and call that interval 間（あいだ）; the standalone native word fixes Kun あいだ.
Pause silently in the narrow gate opening for one perfectly timed 間（ま）; the standalone native word fixes Kun ま as “time” or a pause.

memory_bridge: Two cans on a string retrieve relational On カン; the traveler entangled with the whole gate dispute retrieves native 関わる（かかわる）.

readings.overlay: Hang two cans on a string across the frontier gate to show their relation; can → カン in 関係（かんけい）.
A traveler keeps handling the gate, the guards, and the border dispute until fully involved: 関わる（かかわる）, ‘to be involved.’
A question rolls like a die inside the head until it lands as the discussion topic: die → ダイ in 問題（もんだい）.

memory_bridge: At one meal, lifting the cover causes a SHOCK that retrieves ショク in 食事（しょくじ）. At the ordinary table, the neutral everyday verb is 食べる（たべる）. A ravenous CUCKOO barges in with a long COO and 食う（くう）, the rougher, casual verb. Treat 食う as register-marked, not as a polite synonym to swap in everywhere.

readings.overlay: The diner lifts the food cover and gasps in SHOCK at the 食事（しょくじ）, meal. SHOCK closely retrieves On ショク.
The diner sits at the ordinary table and 食べる（たべる） the meal. This is the neutral, everyday verb “to eat”; the complete word is the anchor, not the mismatched English TABLE.
A ravenous CUCKOO gives a long COO and 食う（くう） the food. COO closely retrieves くう, while the scene marks the verb as rougher and more casual than 食べる.

memory_bridge: The prime minister’s shoe retrieves title-reading シュ; the neck fitted into a cubby retrieves standalone Kun くび.

readings.overlay: The head of government puts on a formal shoe before appearing as 首相（しゅしょう）; shoe → シュ.
A cubby-shaped collar snaps around the neck beneath the face: cubby → くび, the standalone 首（くび）.

memory_bridge: Use the same school tower twice: its 高校（こうこう） sign supplies compound On コウ, while looking from the ground to its roof prompts the complete adjective 高い（たかい）, high.

readings.overlay: The tall structure becomes a school tower labeled 高校（こうこう）. The repeated school compound anchors On コウ.
Crane your neck toward the tower’s roof and call it 高い（たかい）—high. The full adjective, not a “tall kite” splice, carries the reading.

Lay a single letter E along the one unbroken line: English “E” is a close sound hook for yī, held high and level. Canonical yī changes in connected speech to yí before a fourth tone and yì before a first, second, or third.
The upper mark sits above the baseline in 上面; tap down from the top onto it, and let shàng fall with the finger.
A finger points from the ceiling straight down to 下面; xià drops just as sharply to the space below.

The diagonals pull away from the bar with a rejecting “boo,” a close sound hook for canonical bù, “no”; both drop sharply in the fourth tone. Before another fourth tone, bù surfaces as rising bú—so 不是 is heard bú shì without changing the stored reading.
The 𠆢 roof singles out one 丨 line as one 个. A counter’s hand chops down once on falling gè.

memory_bridge: The elephant acts on a tiny stage: a spotlight points down to the cause in 因为, wèi; then the elephant rises into a new role in 成为, wéi.

readings.overlay: A spotlight points down at why the elephant acted: 因为—because. Wèi drops with the beam onto the cause.
The elephant rises onto a platform and 成为—becomes—the star; wéi climbs with the transformation.
A 丿 slash opens the 厶 secret, but the question 什么—what?—trails off before revealing it; final me is only a light, neutral murmur.
The hooked last stroke reaches out to pull one more guest into the group: 也（yě）, “also.” Let yě dip low, then curl upward like the hook.

memory_bridge: At the finished-work table, the child’s light le closes the task; the inspector then bends over the result and rises with understanding, giving third-tone liǎo in 了解.

readings.overlay: The child tucks in both arms when the work is 了—complete—and a small neutral le settles at the end of the action.
The inspector bends low over the finished work, then straightens as he 了解—understands it; liǎo follows that dip and recovery.
A hand grips the marker for the 事情—the matter at hand—then stamps it decisively onto the case file; shì falls with the stamp.
From 此, take two small steps and set down 一些（yī xiē） snacks—“some,” not all—along one high, level shelf for xiē.
A wren lands on the two-legged 人, then flutters upward to join 人们. ‘Wren’ cues rén, and the bird’s climb fixes the rising tone.
A 亻 person counts 十 possibilities and lifts the last card in a question: 什么—what? Shén rises with the card.
A 亻 person steps beside 也 and the group points to him in 他们. Keep tā on one high, level note over his head.
A person bends under a shoulder strap, then straightens by means of it; 可以 gives permission to use it, while yǐ follows the dip and recovery.
One 亻 person after another passes through 门／門 mén until they form a group. The gate supplies the sound family, while the plural marker relaxes to neutral men in 我们.

memory_bridge: At one 会 meeting, a raffle ticket drops a 机会 opportunity into your hand—huì; across the table, the 会计 accountant closes the ledger on kuài. Each reading has its own station in the room.

readings.overlay: Under the meeting roof, a raffle ticket drops a lucky 机会—chance—into your hand; huì falls with the ticket.
Across that room, the 会计 accountant totals the greetings and snaps the ledger shut; kuài falls with the cover.
At dawn the person should rise—but the blanket comes down again. Put 但是（dàn shì）, “but,” on that reversal, and let dàn fall with the blanket.
The 亻 person faces 尔—you—and drops to one knee before you. ‘Knee’ cues nǐ; the kneel and recovery trace its third tone.
A worker finishes 做事 and stamps the job DONE; the stamp slams downward with fourth-tone zuò.
A little 儿子 climbs upward into a parent’s arms; ér rises with the son.
The sprout pushes through the receptacle and keeps coming 出来（chū lái）, “to come out”; hold chū high and level as it clears the opening.

memory_bridge: Let the knife cut two contrasting pieces: it separates 别人, “other people,” with rising bié; the oddly twisted offcut becomes 别扭, “awkward,” with falling biè. The clean piece and warped piece make the tone contrast visible.

readings.overlay: The knife cuts another group away and you point upward toward 别人（bié ren）, “others”; bié rises along the gesture.
The crooked offcut twists into a chair that feels 别扭（biè niu）, “awkward”; biè drops as you collapse out of it.
At 到达, the runner reaches the finish and a knife cuts the ribbon downward; dào falls with the cut.
Bury the secret, leave the place, and watch the old calendar page drop into 过去—the past; qù falls away with it.

memory_bridge: Split simplified 发 into its two traditional identities: 發 emits a discovery flag in 发现 with high-level fā; 髮 is a strand of hair, whose citation reading is falling fà, though 头发 commonly realizes that syllable lightly as tóu fa. The flag and hair strand prevent the merged shape from merging the readings.

readings.overlay: The hand flicks a discovery flag outward as the detective shouts 发现（fā xiàn）, “found it”; hold fā high and level. This sense corresponds to traditional 發.
A strand of 头发（tóu fa）, “hair,” falls from the head. Remember the dictionary form as falling fà and traditional 髮, while the anchor word’s second syllable is commonly light fa.

memory_bridge: One mouth under a spotlight first narrows a claim to 只是, “merely,” with dipping zhǐ; then the light lands on one animal counted with high-level zhī. In traditional writing, the classifier is 隻 while “merely” remains 只, which keeps the two roles visibly distinct.

readings.overlay: With every other mouth silent, 只是（zhǐ shì） shrinks the claim to “merely” this; the voice dips low on zhǐ, then edges back up.
A zookeeper counts one animal under a steady spotlight—one 只（zhī）, high and level. This classifier is written 隻 in traditional text.
The 口 mouth lowers its voice to consider the request, then lifts into permission: 可以—you can. Kě follows that dip and recovery.
After the crowned 后 queen gives her command, the next courtier arrives 后来（hòu lái）, “later”; hòu falls like the curtain between scenes. In traditional writing, this later sense appears as 後來.
The 口 mouth borrows the 马／馬 mǎ sound family, then turns it into a yes-or-no question. In 吗, the syllable sheds the horse’s tone and lands as light, neutral ma.
A mouth lets 巴 cling softly to the end of a command, cushioning it into a suggestion; 吧, neutral ba, is barely heavier than a sigh.
The axe splits speech from the mouth just as a bell rings “ting”; everyone leans in to 听说（tīng shuō）, “hear what is said.” Stretch the close bell cue high and level into tīng.

memory_bridge: At one table, a rising ‘HUH?’ settles 和平 as hé; by the stove, warm breath leaves 暖和 with light huo.

readings.overlay: At the grain-laden peace table, one mouth starts an argument. The other tilts upward and asks ‘HUH?’; that rising HUH recalls rising-tone hé before they agree on 和平（hé píng）, ‘peace.’
Beside that table, a stove warms the grain room until it is 暖和（nuǎn huo）, ‘warm’; keep this common word as the anchor for the light, unstressed final huo.
The mouth opens on the slope and an echo slips out—啊（a）! Keep the exclamation short, light, and unstressed.
A call circles the enclosure as an echo, then 回来（huí lai）, “returns,” to the mouth; huí rises as the sound comes back.
Stamp the 土 earth under your feet to mark 现在—right now. Zài drops firmly onto the exact place and moment.
One dusk follows another until there are too many to count; a calendar asks 多少（duō shao）, “how many?” Keep duō high and level across the accumulating evenings.

memory_bridge: In the town square, 大家 is the big crowd shouting dà; the person treating that crowd is 大夫, the doctor called dài fu.

readings.overlay: A huge town square fills with 大家—everyone—and the conductor chops his baton down on dà.
An enormous doctor labeled 大夫 drops a prescription into your hand; that special medical title begins with falling dài.
今天 stretches overhead like a clear horizon; keep tiān high and level across today’s sky.
The 大 big figure adds one extra dot as a tie tack and becomes 太（tài）, “too; overly” dressed. English “tie” closely cues tài, and the necktie drops sharply to mark the fourth tone.
A 女 woman stands beside 也 while 她们 point to their group. Hold tā high and level over her head.

memory_bridge: In the woman-and-child scene, a visitor kneels and rises while greeting them 你好, hǎo; afterward they pin up an 爱好 hobby poster with a decisive downward thump, hào.

readings.overlay: A visitor sees the 女 woman and 子 child together, bows low, then rises with 你好. Hǎo follows the greeting’s dip and recovery.
The pair proudly pin their 爱好 hobby poster to the wall; the final tack lands downward with fourth-tone hào.
The woman shapes her mouth to match the portrait beside a fork sign reading 如果（rú guǒ）, “if”; rú rises toward the possible likeness.

马／馬 is the authentic sound-bearing component in 妈／媽 and preserves the ma syllable family; 妈妈（mā ma）, “mama,” fixes the modern first-tone reading. Picture the mother calming the horse with one high, level mā, followed by a light second ma.

memory_bridge: At one playground, a child raises and lowers both arms for full zǐ in 子女; when the same child runs after 孩 in 孩子, zi becomes a light suffix tagging along behind.

readings.overlay: The 子女 child lowers both raised arms, then throws them back up; the gesture traces full third-tone zǐ.
The child runs after 孩 and tags along in 孩子; final zi is light and neutral, like the smaller footsteps behind.
The straight foot points to one roof and a judge declares 一定（citation yī dìng）, “certainly”; the gavel and dìng both drop with finality. In ordinary speech, 一 surfaces as yí before fourth-tone dìng.

memory_bridge: Keep the pig beneath one roof: pull back to include 大家, “everyone,” and 家 is high-level jiā; step softly into 人家, a household, and 家 becomes neutral jia. The wide group shot and quiet interior keep the readings distinct.

readings.overlay: The roof expands over the pig and the whole community in 大家（dà jiā）, “everyone”; hold jiā high and level across the broad roofline.
Step quietly beneath the roof of 人家（rén jia）, “a household”; the final jia is soft and unstressed, like taking off your shoes indoors.
The hand adjusts the inch measure until it is 对—right—then the worker bows down in 对不起 to apologize; duì falls with the bow.
Between the two small side dots, a careful walker takes a tiny step: 小心（xiǎo xīn）, “be careful.” The foot dips to test the ground, then rises safely with xiǎo.
The capital summons its remarkable leader, who arrives 就是 at precisely the right moment; a seal drops onto jiù to certify ‘exactly so.’
At 开始, a starting gate swings wide and stays open; hold kāi high and level as the race begins.

memory_bridge: Use the little snout-stamp twice: an authentic stamp confirms 当然, “of course,” with high-level dāng; a counterfeit stamp springs a trap in 上当, “be fooled,” with falling dàng. Real confirmation and deception sharply separate the readings.

readings.overlay: The little snout works as a stamp and certifies 当然（dāng rán）, “of course”; hold dāng high and level across the genuine seal.
A trickster swaps in a false stamp and you 上当（shàng dàng）, “are fooled”; dàng drops with the trapdoor beneath the seal.
A stubborn hen blocks the 彳 path; it crouches low, then springs back up. ‘Hen’ cues hěn, and the motion fixes its third tone in 很—quite.

memory_bridge: One traveler reaches a prize: he lifts it with rising dé when he 得到 it, slumps and recovers on děi when he must take the last step, then hangs a nearly weightless de tag after the completed action.

readings.overlay: The traveler takes the final step, 得到 the prize, and lifts it overhead; dé rises with what he obtains.
The path sign says 总得—must—so the traveler slumps low, then gets back up; děi traces that reluctant third tone.
After the action, a tiny structural 得 tag hangs from the verb to describe how it happened; neutral de is almost weightless.
小心: a monitor draws one steady high line over the heart while you stay careful; hold xīn high and level.
Trying the task for the first time, the worried heart bends toward the instructions, then looks up and asks 怎么（zěn me）, “how?” Let zěn dip and recover with that motion.
相 supplies the sound family above 心. The heart sinks deep in thought, then lifts with a 想法—an idea—tracing third-tone xiǎng.
A sound rises from the heart, becomes an 意思（yì si）, “idea,” and drops decisively onto the page; yì falls with that moment of meaning.
The lone speaker startles at the forked blade—“whoa!”—then taps his chest: 我, me. English “whoa” is a close hook for wǒ; his voice drops with the blade and curls back up in the third tone.
At the woodcutting place, an arrow leads from the axe-marked reason to the door-marked result: 所以（suǒ yǐ）, “therefore.” Let suǒ dive under the reason, then curve up toward the conclusion.
A nail jams the lid, so the hand taps it down, then levers the box 打开（dǎ kāi）, “open”; dǎ follows that dip-and-rise motion.
Grip a handle with 把: your hand closes downward, then lifts the object, tracing the dip and recovery of bǎ.
On a 时间 clock, the sun climbs while its shadow lengthens inch by inch; shí rises with the passing time.
Even when a challenger interrupts with 但是—but—the straight foot stays planted beneath the sun. The judge stamps down a verdict on shì: it is so.
The left hand tries to possess the 月 flesh, but a yo-yo marked 没有 drops from its grip and returns. ‘Yo’ cues yǒu, and the toy traces the third-tone dip and recovery.
On a horizon labeled 未来, the future comes toward you and rises into view; lái climbs as it approaches.
At the 如果 fork, a fruit drops low as you weigh ‘if,’ then bobs back up; guǒ traces its swing.
A carver stamps the sheep-shaped model onto each wooden piece so they come out 一样—the same; yàng falls with the stamp.

memory_bridge: One hand tool vanishes into the water: above the surface, the searcher’s call rises on méi because there isn’t any; below it, the tool sinks with falling mò in 沉没.

readings.overlay: Water sweeps the hand tool away, so the searcher calls 没有—there isn’t any—with rising méi.
The lost tool continues beneath the surface and 沉没—sinks; mò falls with it into the water.

Only 一点（citation yī diǎn）, “a bit,” of ash remains above the fortune-telling fire; your finger dips to the tiny speck, then lifts with diǎn. In ordinary speech, 一 surfaces as yì before third-tone diǎn.
When the old fire scene finishes, 然后（rán hòu） introduces what happens “then; afterward”; rán rises like the next scene lifting into view.
见／見 is the authentic sound-bearing component and shares the -iàn rhyme with 现／現. Bring the jade into view at 现在（xiàn zài）, “now,” and let xiàn fall as the covering cloth drops away.
A sprout bursts through the ground and holds one high, level note as 生活—life—begins; keep shēng on that growing line.
Pull a tool from one section of the divided 使用（shǐ yòng） box, “use” it, then drop it firmly onto the workbench; yòng lands with the tool.

memory_bridge: The bullseye carries two paper tags: a feather-light ownership tag marked de clings to it; an inspector then raises a confirmation flag for 的确, where dí means ‘really.’

readings.overlay: A tiny ownership label clings to the 白 center of the 勺 target; it is so light that 的 is only neutral de.
An inspector checks the bullseye and lifts a green flag: 的确, really. Dí rises with the confirming flag.

memory_bridge: The hand over the eye has two jobs: it drops as you look and 看见, kàn; it stays rigidly level through a guard’s 看守, kān.

readings.overlay: Drop the hand over the eye and look down until you 看见 the scene; kàn falls with the visor.
A guard holds the same hand-visor perfectly level throughout 看守; kān stays high and even through the watch.
A truth scanner shines one unwavering beam across 真的; hold zhēn high and level because the answer is really true.

memory_bridge: Keep the sheep and watching eye in one short film: the eye keeps watching 着 with light zhe; the sheep disappears and the watcher grows 着急 with rising zháo; then the watcher rolls up their sleeves and 着手 with rising zhuó. The changing event distinguishes ongoing aspect, worry, and setting to work.

readings.overlay: The eye keeps watching the approaching sheep 着（zhe）, marking an action in progress; neutral zhe is a light background beat that never takes focus.
When the sheep vanishes, the watcher becomes 着急（zháo jí）, “worried”; zháo rises like the alarm in their voice.
The watcher rolls up their sleeves and 着手（zhuó shǒu）, “sets out” to search; zhuó rises as their hands lift toward the task.
A mouth fires a dart-straight answer across a high, level line: 知道—to know. Hold zhī as steady as the dart’s flight.
A timeline thread held straight in the warp shows the clock has 已经（yǐ jīng）, “already,” reached its mark; keep jīng high and level along the taut thread.

memory_bridge: Use one thread-wrapped parcel in two scenes: a hand gives it directly with everyday 给（gěi）; a warehouse line repeatedly furnishes parcels in 供给（gōng jǐ）. Both readings dip and recover, but direct giving and formal supplying remain distinct.

readings.overlay: The wrapping thread fits snugly as you lower the parcel into another person’s hands: 给（gěi）, “to give.” Your hand returns upward as gěi completes its dip.
At the 供给（gōng jǐ） depot, “to furnish,” a forklift dips beneath the wrapped crate and raises it onto the supply line, tracing third-tone jǐ.
The tiny worm proves its 能力 by tracing every curve of the seal; its capability meter rises with néng when it finishes.
In the mirror, you point firmly down at 自己—oneself—and zì lands with the gesture.

memory_bridge: Follow one 行-marked route through two supporting words: 行动 labels the uphill action stop for xíng, while 银行 labels the bank stop for háng. Both readings rise, but the words keep their meanings and syllables distinct.

readings.overlay: Use 行动（xíng dòng）, “action,” as the supporting word for xíng; the team’s uphill march only traces the second-tone rise.
Use 银行（yín háng）, “bank,” as the supporting word for háng; the route’s climb toward the vault only traces the second-tone rise.

memory_bridge: Under the same cover, a needed object is pulled down for 需要, yào; when it becomes a formal 要求 request, the woman holds it overhead on level yāo.

readings.overlay: The woman finds what she 需要 under the cover and pulls the needed object down; yào falls with it.
She turns the object into a written 要求 and holds the request overhead; yāo stays high and level until someone answers.
The eye on human legs turns toward a stage; when the curtain drops, it suddenly 看见（kàn jiàn）, “sees,” the scene, and jiàn falls at that instant.

memory_bridge: Keep the eyes open for 觉得, where a thought rises with jué; close them onto the pillow for 睡觉, where jiào falls into sleep. The awake and asleep frames make both pronunciation and meaning contrastive.

readings.overlay: With eyes open, a thought bubble rises over 觉得（jué de）, “to think”; jué climbs with the idea.
Close the eyes and let your head drop onto the pillow to 睡觉（shuì jiào）, “sleep”; jiào falls as you fall asleep.
The guard raises one speaker’s argument above the other, then orders 让开（ràng kāi）, “step aside”; his barrier drops in one firm fourth-tone ràng.
In 说话, each spoken word falls from the mouth into the listener’s ear; huà lands with that downward stroke.
An obligation sign stays fixed overhead: 应该—ought to. Hold gāi high and level like the rule that will not move.
During a 兑 exchange of 讠 speech, the speaker holds one bright speech bubble high and level: shuō in 说话.
As offers shoot toward you, answer with 谢谢（xiè xie）, “thank you,” and lower your head; the first xiè falls with the bow while the second syllable stays light.
Use 走路（zǒu lù）, “to walk,” as the supporting word for zǒu; the foot’s earth path only traces its third-tone dip and recovery, without pretending to supply the syllable.
Your 己 self crouches at the start of the walking path, then gets 起来（qǐ lai）, “up”; qǐ dips with the crouch and rises with the body.

memory_bridge: A needle makes one journey through the cloth: while it passes, guò falls out the far side in 过去; afterward, only a light guo experience-tag remains stitched to the event.

readings.overlay: The needle travels 过去 through every inch of cloth, then drops out the far side; guò falls with the completed passage.
Once the needle has been through, a tiny 过 tag remains to mark the experience; guo is light and neutral because the journey is backgrounded.

memory_bridge: At a fork, the traveler raises one hand toward the path he is still considering—还是, hái; after choosing, he turns back and lifts the borrowed parcel to its owner—偿还, huán.

readings.overlay: At the fork, the traveler is 还是 deciding—this or that—and raises a hand toward the second path; hái rises with the choice.
The traveler turns around and lifts the borrowed parcel back to its owner in 偿还; huán rises with the repayment.
⻌ movement delivers 文 writing to one exact spot; point down at 这个—this one—and let zhè fall with the finger.
Follow the head along the road until it points down at the answer: 知道—to know. Dào falls on the place where the way becomes clear.
Remove the questioning 口 from 哪 and point away: “Nah—that one over there.” English “nah” is a close sound hook for nà, and the pointing hand drops sharply with its fourth tone toward 那里.

memory_bridge: Enter one city scene: all the residents hold a single high line for dōu; at the center, the 首都 capital tower holds its own high line for dū.

readings.overlay: Every person in the city raises one level banner for 都—all; dōu stays high and flat across the whole crowd.
At the crowd’s center, the 首都 capital tower rises to the same steady height; dū names the capital itself.
Cross the field-and-earth path, descend through the gate, then come back up 里面—inside. The route traces third-tone lǐ.
